malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Victims who clicked the malicious link were redirected to a phishing website asking for their cPanel credentials.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user clicks the phishing link in the email, the browser is redirected to a fake cPanel login page that collects entered credentials and sends them to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The website mimics a legitimate cPanel login page to steal user credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate security advisories do not ask users to enter credentials on non-official domains; credential collection should only occur on trusted, official sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate password reset or login pages, but only on official domains.
key_indicators: Fake login page hosted on non-cPanel domain

execution_context.trigger: runtime (Magecart skimmer executes in browser when user visits checkout page)
execution_context.file_location: injected JavaScript on e-commerce checkout pages (via homoglyph domain or favicon)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: A new credit card skimming campaign making use of homoglyph – domain lookalike – techniques has been connected to an existing Magecart threat group that utilizes the inter kit and favicon to hide skimming activity and lure a victim into purchasing on malicious websites.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, injected JavaScript code reads credit card input fields on the checkout page, then exfiltrates the data to an attacker-controlled server, often using obfuscated or hidden requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code surreptitiously collects sensitive payment data and sends it to an external server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce sites should not exfiltrate payment data to third-party domains or hide code in favicons.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts, but only to trusted vendors.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into checkout pages
Use of homoglyph domains and favicon-based hiding

attack_chain.action: Phishing email sent to cPanel users with a fake security advisory and malicious link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User clicks link and is redirected to phishing website.

attack_chain.action: Phishing website collects cPanel credentials entered by the victim.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's cPanel account.

attack_chain.action: Magecart skimmer JavaScript is injected into e-commerce checkout pages on homoglyph or lookalike domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Skimmer executes when user visits checkout page.

attack_chain.action: Skimmer reads credit card data from DOM and exfiltrates it to attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing emails with urgent security advisories and links to non-official domains
Web pages mimicking cPanel login on non-cPanel domains
JavaScript accessing payment fields and sending data to external domains
Obfuscated or hidden JavaScript in favicons or third-party scripts
file_indicators: Phishing email templates referencing cPanel vulnerabilities
network_indicators: Outbound requests to domains similar to legitimate brands (homoglyphs)
POST requests from checkout pages to unknown or suspicious domains
Phishing sites hosted on recently registered or lookalike domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for phishing emails with suspicious links, especially those referencing urgent security issues. Flag login pages for sensitive services (like cPanel) hosted on non-official domains. Scan e-commerce sites for injected or obfuscated JavaScript, especially in favicons or third-party scripts, that accesses payment fields and sends data to external servers. Monitor network traffic for POST requests to domains not associated with legitimate payment processors or service providers.
